name: Kensey Johns
bio: a Representative from Delaware; born in New Castle, New Castle County, Del., December 10, 1791; pursued classical studies and graduated from Princeton College in 1810; studied law; was admitted to the bar in 1813 and commenced practice in New Castle; elected as an Adams candidate to the Twentieth Congress, by special election, to fill the vacancy caused by the resignation of Louis McLane; reelected as an Anti-Jacksonian candidate to the Twenty-first Congress (October 2, 1827-March 3, 1831); was not a candidate for renomination in 1830 to the Twenty-second Congress; appointed chancellor of Delaware in 1832 and served until his death in New Castle, Del., on March 28, 1857; interment in the Presbyterian Cemetery.
